classification.difficultyReason: Translate coordinates into useful lengths or a geometric decomposition, then connect that representation to an area method; the cosine-rule route links distance, exact sine and area calculations.

content.prompt: Points $A(3,4)$ and $B(12,-5)$ form a triangle with the origin $O$. Find the area of $\triangle AOB$.

inlines.text: Find the side lengths, use the cosine rule to obtain
, then find the sine and apply the area rule.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta=\angle AOB$.
$$\begin{align*}OA&=\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5\\OB&=\sqrt{12^2+(-5)^2}=13\\AB^2&=(12-3)^2+(-5-4)^2=162\end{align*}$$
By the cosine rule,
$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{5^2+13^2-162}{2(5)(13)}\\\cos\theta&=\frac{16}{65}\end{align*}$$
Since $\cos\theta>0$, $\theta$ is acute. In an auxiliary right triangle with adjacent side 16 and hypotenuse 65, the opposite side is
$$\begin{align*}\text{opposite side}&=\sqrt{65^2-16^2}\\\text{opposite side}&=63\end{align*}$$
Hence,
$$\begin{align*}\sin\theta&=\frac{63}{65}\\\operatorname{Area}(\triangle AOB)&=\frac12(5)(13)\left(\frac{63}{65}\right)\\\operatorname{Area}(\triangle AOB)&=\frac{63}{2}\text{ square units}\\\operatorname{Area}(\triangle AOB)&=31.5\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$
